newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany slams Belgrade for curtailing democracy.
newsitem.headline: Germany slams Belgrade for curtailing democracy.

text.p: German Foreign Minister Klaus Kinkel criticised Belgrade on Wednesday for shutting an independent radio station and warned Serbian authorities the world was closely watching how they handled pro-democracy protests.
Kinkel described the Yugoslav situation as worrying and pledged to discuss the subject at an international conference on Bosnia in London which opened on Wednesday.

"Freedom to assemble and freedom of speech, pluralism and free media are the cornerstones of every democratic society. Whoever jeopardises these freedoms must pay the consequences. The government in Belgrade must know this," Kinkel said.

Germany's official short-wave radio broadcaster, Deutsche Welle, said on Wednesday it would start transmitting some of Radio B-92's reports on events in Belgrade and other Serbian towns during its daily Serbian programme.
Deutsche Welle director Dieter Weirich said the closure "ran against the universal principals of press freedom.
"Deutsche Welle declares its solidarity with its colleagues at Radio B-92 and all other Serbian journalists who are fighting for the freedom of the media," he said in a statement.

Tens of thousands of people have been marching through the frozen streets of Belgrade to protest against the annulling of local election results last month by the socialist rulers after opposition parties won sweeping victories.
The United States condemned the closure of Radio B-92 and called for a concerted international campaign against Belgrade's "anti-democratic" actions.

State Department officials listed measures they said would stay in force until Serbia changed its ways but made clear they had no plans at present to seek to re-impose full trade sanctions on Belgrade lifted by the United Nations last year.

A final communique from a European security summit in Lisbon criticising Belgrade was watered down after Russia defended Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic and insisted on striking out a call for Serbian democracy.
